newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends week buoyant, others firmer.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends week buoyant, others firmer.

text.p: Copper surged to fresh highs over $2,000 on Friday afternoon, but aluminium lost some momentum after two days of sharp gains.
Three months copper ended the kerb at a fresh seven-week high of $2,028 per tonne, a gain of $35 from Thursday and $80 since the start of the week.
It was a fresh peak since September 5 when prices hit $2,037, which some analysts peg as the next target.
Prices had hovered around the $2,000 level all day after stocks fell by hefty 13,525 tonnes, but finally broke loose of the psychological area on the afternoon kerb.
Prices wavered during the day as players were nervous of the market being hit by end-of-week profit-taking, producer selling and bank liquidation of left-over Sumitomo positions.
After $2,037, the next area the market is expected to focus on is the $2,070 high of September 4.
The physical market remains tight with the premium of cash over three months metal firming slightly to $35/$40.
Aluminium, however, failed to match copper's gains, never regaining a $1,441 high hit early on Friday.
Prices lost steam after stocks declined by only 3,600 tonnes, much lower than rumoured figures.
But the market ended in positive territory, up $10.50, and if stocks continue to erode next week, analysts say the market could continue to make more progress.
Prices would have to surmount important resistance at $1,440 to trigger sustained gains, chartists say.
This level signifies recent highs as well as where the May downtrend intersects, chartists said.
Copper's rally lifted the others into scoring gains.
Nickel broke through $7,250 resistance, which was the high of October 8, finishing $40 higher at $7,270.
Next resistance was seen at $7,310.
Zinc ended the kerb at its high of $1,039, up $12, after breaching $1,032 resistance and its end-July downtrend line.
It was the highest level since September 19, with the next goal pegged at $1,056.
Lead and tin failed to share the joy, ending little changed, with lead up $1 at $738 and tin $10 firmer at $5,990.
Last business in alloy was up $2 at $1,282.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8065
